meta.name: Turn Fireflies meeting transcripts into ClickUp tasks, Sheets logs, Gmail and Slack alerts with OpenAI

name: Meeting intelligence from Fireflies: tasks, summary, Slack and alerts

nodes.name: Meeting finished
nodes.notes:
Receives a POST from Fireflies when a meeting transcript is ready.

Setup:
1. Activate this workflow to get the webhook URL
2. Copy the Production URL shown below the node
3. In Fireflies: Settings → Developer Settings → Webhooks → Add new
4. Paste the URL and select event: Transcription completed
5. Save — Fireflies will now call this URL after every meeting

Fireflies sends the meeting ID in the webhook body.
This workflow then fetches the full transcript via their API.

nodes.name: Set config
nodes.notes:
REPLACE ALL THESE VALUES:

1. firefliesApiKey
   Fireflies → Settings → Developer Settings → API Key

2. clickupApiKey
   ClickUp → Profile → Apps → API Token
   NOTE: ClickUp API uses the token directly in the Authorization header
   Do NOT add the word Bearer before it

3. clickupListId
   Open your target ClickUp list in browser
   URL format: app.clickup.com/123/v/l/456789
   The last number is your List ID

4. managerEmail
   Who receives the negative sentiment alert
   Example: you@example.com

5. slackChannelId
   Open Slack in browser → click on the channel
   URL format: app.slack.com/client/T.../C01234ABCDE
   The C... part is the Channel ID

6. sheetId
   Google Sheet URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123/edit
   Copy the part between /d/ and /edit

7. teamName
   Your company or team name — appears in meeting summaries
   Example: Incrementors

8. senderName
   Your name for email sign-offs
   Example: Rahul Dutt

nodes.name: Get the meeting ID
nodes.notes:
Extracts the meeting ID from the Fireflies webhook body.
Throws a clear error if the meeting ID is missing
so you can troubleshoot the webhook connection.

Also carries all config values forward.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Fetch the transcript
nodes.notes:
Fetches the complete transcript from Fireflies API using GraphQL.

Endpoint: POST https://api.fireflies.ai/graphql
Auth: Bearer token from your Fireflies API key

Fetches:
- Full transcript with speaker labels
- AI filters (task, pricing, question flags per sentence)
- Summary: overview, keywords, action items
- Analytics: sentiment percentages, speaker talk time

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Tidy the transcript
nodes.notes:
Processes the Fireflies API response into structured, usable data.

Extracts:
- Readable transcript with speaker names
- Sentences flagged as pricing or budget mentions
- All questions asked during the meeting
- Speaker participation percentages and word counts
- Sentiment breakdown (positive, negative, neutral percentages)
- Meeting duration, date, and participants

Calculates sentiment label:
- Negative: negative_pct above 30%
- Mixed: negative_pct between 15% and 30%
- Positive: positive_pct above 60%
- Neutral: everything else

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Extract the intelligence
nodes.notes:
First AI agent — extracts structured meeting intelligence.

Outputs 7 fields:
1. actionItems — with owner, priority, and deadline
2. sentimentAnalysis — client mood, concerns, positives
3. keyTopics — main topics discussed
4. competitorsMentioned — any competitor names
5. hasCompetitorMention — boolean flag for routing
6. nextMeetingNeeded — whether follow-up was requested
7. meetingSuccessScore — 1 to 10 meeting quality score

All fields enforced by Intel Output Parser below.
Output is in $json.output

parameters.text:
=You are a senior client success analyst for {{ $json.teamName }}.

Analyze this meeting transcript and extract structured intelligence.

Meeting: {{ $json.meetingTitle }}
Date: {{ $json.meetingDate }}
Duration: {{ $json.durationMin }} minutes
Participants: {{ $json.participants }}

Fireflies AI overview: {{ $json.aiOverview }}
Fireflies action items summary: {{ $json.aiActionItems }}

Full transcript:
{{ $json.fullText }}

Pricing or budget sentences flagged:
{{ $json.pricingSentences.join('\n') || 'None detected' }}

Return ONLY a valid JSON object. No extra text. No markdown. No backticks.

Required fields:

actionItems
Array of objects from this meeting. Each has:
  task: specific action item under 20 words
  owner: person responsible (use speaker name from transcript, or Team if unclear)
  priority: exactly one of High, Medium, or Low
  deadline: date or timeframe mentioned in the meeting, or null if none given

sentimentAnalysis
Object with:
  overallSentiment: exactly one of Positive, Negative, Mixed, or Neutral
  clientMood: one sentence on how the client seemed during this meeting
  concernsRaised: array of specific concerns or objections the client mentioned
  positives: array of things the client responded positively to

keyTopics
Array of 3 to 5 strings. The main business topics discussed.

competitorsMentioned
Array of strings. Names of any competitor products, services, or companies mentioned.
Empty array if none.

hasCompetitorMention
Boolean. True if any competitor was explicitly named.

nextMeetingNeeded
Boolean. True if the transcript suggests a follow-up meeting should be scheduled.

meetingSuccessScore
Number from 1 to 10. How productive and positive was this meeting overall?
1 to 3 means difficult with unresolved issues.
4 to 6 means average with some progress.
7 to 8 means good with clear next steps.
9 to 10 means excellent with strong alignment.

nodes.name: Chat model - Intelligence
nodes.notes:
Connect your OpenAI API credential here.

1. Go to platform.openai.com/api-keys
2. Create a new key
3. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → OpenAI API
4. Connect to this node

temperature: 0.2 for precise extraction
Cost: about $0.003 per meeting analyzed

nodes.name: Output Parser - Intelligence
nodes.notes:
Schema: 7 required fields for meeting intelligence.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Prepare the deliverables
nodes.notes:
Combines meeting data and AI intelligence into one complete record.

Prepares:
- Formatted action items list for ClickUp task description
- Concerns and positives as pipe-separated strings for Sheets
- ClickUp task title and priority (urgent if negative sentiment)
- Routing flag: needsManagerAlert = true when sentiment is Negative or Mixed

All downstream nodes read from this node using:
$('Prepare the deliverables').item.json

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Create the ClickUp task
nodes.notes:
Creates a ClickUp task with all action items from the meeting.

Task includes:
- Meeting title and date in task name
- All action items with owners, priorities, and deadlines
- Key topics covered
- Meeting recording link (if available)

ClickUp API priority values:
1 = Urgent (negative sentiment meetings)
2 = Normal (standard meetings)
3 = Low (high success score meetings)

IMPORTANT:
ClickUp API does NOT use Bearer prefix.
The API key goes directly in the Authorization header.
This is different from most other APIs.

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Log to the sheet
nodes.notes:
Logs every meeting to Google Sheets as a permanent intelligence record.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable Google Sheets API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Google Sheets OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

Sheet tab: Meeting Intelligence
Row 1 headers:
Date | Meeting Title | Duration | Participants | Overall Sentiment | Client Mood | Action Items Count | Key Topics | Competitors Mentioned | Success Score | Logged At

Use this sheet to:
- Track meeting quality scores over time
- Spot clients with recurring negative sentiment
- Build a competitor mention tracker
- Calculate average meeting success rates per client

nodes.name: Write the summary
nodes.notes:
Second AI agent — writes the professional meeting summary email.

This agent uses the structured data from the first agent.
It writes in natural language, not bullet points.

The summary references:
- What was actually discussed (from key topics)
- Agreed action items with owners
- Client sentiment and concerns (handled diplomatically)
- Next steps

Output is in $json.output (plain text email body)

nodes.name: Chat model - Summary
nodes.notes:
Connect the same OpenAI credential here.
temperature: 0.5 for natural-sounding professional writing
Cost: about $0.002 per summary

nodes.name: Format the messages
nodes.notes:
Builds all outgoing messages in one place:
1. Gmail subject and body for participant summary
2. Slack debrief message for team channel
3. Manager alert email body (used if sentiment is negative)
4. Competitor intelligence alert email body (used if competitor mentioned)

All messages reference $('Prepare the deliverables') for consistent data.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Email the summary
nodes.notes:
Sends the AI-written meeting summary to the meeting host.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable the Gmail API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Gmail OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

Sends to the meeting host email from Fireflies.
To CC all participants, use the additionalFields → CC field
and set it to: $('Prepare the deliverables').item.json.participants

nodes.name: Post the team debrief
nodes.notes:
Posts the meeting debrief to your Slack team channel.

How to connect:
1. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Slack OAuth2
2. Authenticate with your Slack workspace
3. Connect to this node

The Slack message includes:
- Meeting title, date, duration
- Sentiment and success score
- First 3 action items (others are in ClickUp)
- Key topics
- Competitor flag if applicable
- Recording link

nodes.name: Sentiment a concern?
nodes.notes:
TRUE — sentiment is Negative or Mixed — send manager alert
FALSE — sentiment is Positive or Neutral — no escalation needed

Reads needsManagerAlert from Prepare All Deliverables.
Change the threshold by editing the Process Transcript node:
Change negativePct threshold from 15 to 20 for less sensitive alerts.
No changes needed here.

nodes.name: Alert the manager
nodes.notes:
Sends a manager alert when the meeting sentiment was Negative or Mixed.

Connect the same Gmail credential here.

Email includes:
- Meeting details and sentiment score
- Specific concerns the client raised
- Client mood description
- Recording link for review
- Recommended follow-up action

To change who gets this alert, update managerEmail in Set Config Values.

parameters.subject: =Client Sentiment Alert — {{ $('Prepare the deliverables').item.json.overallSentiment }} — {{ $('Prepare the deliverables').item.json.meetingTitle }}

nodes.name: Competitor mentioned?
nodes.notes:
TRUE — a competitor was named in this meeting — send intelligence alert
FALSE — no competitor mentioned — no alert needed

Reads hasCompetitorMention from Prepare All Deliverables.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Send the competitor alert
nodes.notes:
Sends a competitor intelligence alert when a competitor is named during a meeting.

Connect the same Gmail credential here.

Email includes:
- Which competitor was mentioned
- Meeting context and participants
- Key topics from the meeting
- Recommended next action

This helps your team prepare a competitive response before the client's next interaction.

nodes.name: Done
nodes.notes:
Final node — marks the meeting as fully processed.
Summary of what was done:
- Full transcript fetched from Fireflies API
- Action items extracted by AI Agent 1
- ClickUp task created with full action item checklist
- Meeting logged to Google Sheets
- Professional summary written by AI Agent 2
- Summary emailed to host via Gmail
- Debrief posted to Slack
- Manager alert sent if sentiment was negative or mixed
- Competitor alert sent if competitor was mentioned

assignments.name: status
assignments.value: =Meeting intelligence processed: {{ $('Prepare the deliverables').item.json.meetingTitle }} — {{ $('Prepare the deliverables').item.json.meetingDate }}

parameters.content:
## 1. Pull the transcript
Fireflies calls this webhook when a recording finishes. One config node holds every key and ID, then the full transcript is fetched and tidied for the model.

## 2. Extract the intelligence
GPT returns action items with owners and priorities, client sentiment, concerns raised and any competitor mentions, all as structured fields.

## 3. Turn it into deliverables
A ClickUp task is created with the action item checklist, the meeting is logged to your sheet, and a second agent writes the summary that goes out to people.

## 4. Send it out and flag risks
The host gets the summary by email and the team gets a Slack debrief. Negative sentiment emails your manager, and a competitor mention sends its own alert.

# Meeting intelligence from Fireflies: tasks, summary, Slack and alerts

When Fireflies finishes transcribing a call, this turns it into everything the team actually needs: a ClickUp task holding the action items, a logged row in your sheet, a written summary emailed to the host, a Slack debrief, and separate alerts when the client sounded unhappy or a competitor came up.

### How it works
1. Fireflies calls the webhook when a recording is ready, and one config node holds every key and ID.
2. The meeting ID is validated, the full transcript is fetched from the Fireflies API, then tidied down for the model.
3. GPT extracts structured intelligence: action items with owners and priorities, client sentiment, concerns raised, and any competitor mentions.
4. Those fields become three things at once: a ClickUp task, a row in your sheet, and the input for a second agent that writes the summary.
5. The host receives the summary by email and your Slack channel gets a team debrief.
6. If sentiment was negative or mixed your manager gets an alert. If a competitor was named, a separate alert goes out.

### Setup
1. Add your OpenAI API key and connect your Google Sheets, Gmail and Slack accounts.
2. In Fireflies open Developer Settings, copy your API key, and point a Transcription completed webhook here.
3. In ClickUp create an API token and copy the list ID from any list URL.
4. Open Set config and replace every placeholder, including your Slack channel ID, manager email and sheet ID.
5. Create a tab called Meeting Intelligence with headers for date, title, duration, participants, sentiment and action item count.

### Customization
Edit the extraction prompt to pull out budget mentions, objections or next meeting dates as well.
